children: The US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved a financing package of up to $1.8 billion for Jordan's $5.8 billion National Water Carrier project, local Arabic-language news channel Al-Mamlaka TV reported on Wednesday.
The package comprises a loan of up to $1 billion and up to $800 million in political risk insurance, according to the report.

The National Water Carrier project, also known as Aqaba-Amman Water Desalination and Conveyance Project (AAWDCP), is a Public Private Partnership (PPP) between Jordan’s Ministry of Water and Irrigation and National Carrier Project Company (NCPC), a special purpose vehicle owned 90 percent by France-based global infrastructure investor Meridiam and 10 percent by Suez.

It involves the design, development, construction, operation and maintenance of a seawater desalination plant, a water transmission system and a dedicated solar power generation facility under a 26-year Design, Build, Finance, Operate, Maintain, and Transfer (DBFOMT) model.
The project will desalinate 300 million cubic metres of seawater annually in Aqaba and transport the water north through a pipeline network extending around 450 kilometres.
Water supply from the project is targeted to begin in 2030.
Jordan's cabinet approved a package of incentives, exemptions and facilities required to implement the project within the Aqaba Special Economic Zone on 17 September.

The project has secured approximately $663 million in grants from international partners, including the United States, European Union, Germany, the Netherlands, United Kingdom, France, Italy, Japan and the Green Climate Fund.
The Jordanian government is contributing $722 million, described as the largest budget allocation for a capital project in the kingdom's history.

The financing plan also includes $2.9 billion in private-sector financing arranged for Meridiam from international financial institutions and local financing of to $1.1 billion from a consortium of commercial banks led by Housing Bank, with participation from the Social Security Investment Fund (SSIF), which is also investing in the project's equity alongside Meridiam.
The government signed the project's final technical and legal agreement in April.
The project is expected to meet around 40 percent of Jordan's drinking water requirements after completion.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
